instruction: Use official Elisity product terminology in all responses. When a user uses a generic industry term, respond with the correct Elisity term but briefly bridge the concept for clarity. Example: 'The Distribution Zone (similar to what you might know as a network zone) defines...'

terms.context: Policy enforcement state where traffic is logged but not blocked. UI actions: 'Save as Simulation'. Enum: MONITOR_ONLY.
Policy enforcement state where traffic is actively permitted/denied. UI actions: 'Activate Policy', 'Save as Active'. Enum: MONITOR_AND_ENFORCE.
Collection of devices receiving the same security treatment. Can be Dynamic or Static, Global or Local.
Reusable L4 traffic filtering template defining protocol, ports, and permit/deny actions.
Visual PG-to-PG grid. Colors: Allow (green), Deny (red), Custom (blue), No Policy (gray).
0-100 metric for policy coverage quality. Also referred to as Policy Deployment Score. Simulation policies contribute only 10% weight.
IEC 62443 aligned criticality. SL1=Low Impact, SL2=Medium, SL3=High, SL4=Critical.
Logical grouping of Virtual Edge Nodes. Software-defined, not a physical appliance.
Existing switch onboarded as an Elisity enforcement point. No new hardware required.

A VEN deployment mode that monitors and reports network traffic without enforcing any policies. Used for pre-deployment network discovery, baselining traffic, and compliance auditing before activating policy enforcement.
Elisity logical enforcement boundary. Can span multiple VLANs.
Dynamic multi-source identity engine that constructs a holistic view of every network entity.
Accept/reject workflow for Insights classification recommendations. Statuses: PENDING, ACCEPTED, REJECTED.
ML/LLM engine for device classification, policy group suggestions, and policy activation recommendations.
System Policy Group where devices land when they don't match any Dynamic or Static Policy Group.
CCC feature for analyzing network traffic flows, top talkers, and policy action breakdowns.
Policy mode where enforcement is handled by an external system. Enum: MONITOR_EXTERNAL.
The AI-powered chat feature in CCC for network security operations assistance.
